newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares surge despite big Agip price slump.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares surge despite big Agip price slump.

text.p: Shares continued their ascent on the Nigerian stock market on Monday despite a big loss by an oil marketer whose shares were adjusted for dividend and bonus issue, traders said.
Due to technical problems the share index was not updated.
Agip shed 3.07 naira because of its recent 35 kobo dividend and a one-for-10 bonus issue, closing at 27.18 naira.
"The fundamentals for the stock, as with other oil shares, remain good," one analyst said.
Investors were not bothered with growing concern following last week's five percent devaluation of the naira, traders said.
"Demand was still strong today; there was no sign that it (devaluation) had any negative impact on trading," said one.
The market's dearest stock, Unipetrol surged 40 kobo to 75.50 naira, ahead of other oil marketers.
African Petroleum closed at 58.30 naira, up 25 kobo, while Texaco rose 20 kobo to 44.50 naira.
Renewed investor interest in Nigerian Breweries cpushed the stock up 70 kobo heave to 17.50 naira. Guinness too strengthened at 8.20 naira, up 10 kobo.
Keen interest in the banking sector saw positive movements among key players, traders said.
Afribank and First Bank advanced 15 kobo each to 7.50 naira and 16.60 naira, respectively, while United Bank for Africa (UBA) added 30 kobo to end at 12.20 naira.

Although profits at tyre maker Dunlop fell to 328.9 million naira by end-1996 compared to 401 million naira in 1995, the company said on Monday it would pay a dividend of 70 kobo and a scrip of one new share for two.
But price of associate DN Meyer, formerly Hagemeyer dipped by five kobo to 4.40 naira.
Textiles group Afprint also fell by one kobo to 2.24 naira on its poor prospects following a recent fire at its wharehouse and falling profitability, dealers said.
